02 / ANATOMY & SPACING

Understand what the line occupies.

The path is only the middle of the stroke. Measure the ink around it, especially where two independent parts come close.

CENTERLINE → VISIBLE INK

A stroke has two sides.

Round caps extend past the endpoints, too. Keep the entire painted stroke inside its envelope and canvas.

A guide for internal detail, not a required empty border around the whole icon.

03 / DESIGN RULES

Build a family resemblance.

These are the library’s current design constraints. The measurements on this page come from the same contracts used to build the icons.

FROM IDEA TO THE GRID

One subject. A clear silhouette. A checked output.

  1. Choose its job. A hosted glyph, a standalone subject, or an enclosure determines the family.
  2. Choose its envelope. Match the subject’s proportions, then draw from its outer bounds inward.
  3. Simplify and check. Keep recognizable details. Inspect the native size, gaps, curves, and joins.
  4. Build and review. Validate geometry and spacing, review the generated output, then add it to the grid. Keep revisions as separate versions; reject the ones you do not want.
